plugins.name: UK Address Postcode Validation
plugins.author: Ideal Postcodes
plugins.short_description: Ideal Postcodes UK address validation and postcode lookup extension for WooCommerce
plugins.description:
Ideal Postcodes adds UK address validation and postcode lookup to WooCommerce.

Help customers enter accurate billing and shipping addresses faster using UK address data from Royal Mail PAF®. Customers can either start typing an address and select a suggestion with Address Finder, or enter a postcode and choose an address with Postcode Lookup.

The plugin works with WooCommerce checkout, billing and shipping forms, My Account address forms and other WooCommerce address forms. Faster address entry reduces typing and address errors while improving the quality of delivery address data.

The WordPress extension is free to install. New Ideal Postcodes accounts include 50 free test credits with no credit card required. Pay-as-you-go address lookup charges apply after the trial. Create an account

Address Finder and Postcode Lookup

Choose the address search experience that works best for your WooCommerce store.

Address Finder

Customers begin typing an address and matching addresses are suggested in real time. Selecting an address automatically fills the relevant WooCommerce address fields.

Postcode Lookup

Customers enter a UK postcode and select their address from a list of matching addresses.

You can enable Address Finder, Postcode Lookup, or both.

Read the WooCommerce setup guide.

Contact us if you get stuck. Drop by our chat page for immediate assistance or send us a message on one of our support channels.

Features

  • Address autocomplete on checkout shipping and billing pages
  • Address autocomplete on accounts pages
  • Post towns now capitalised by default (instead of all caps)
  • Checks if key is usable before enabling autocomplete
  • Optionally populate organisation name from selected address
  • Optionally populate county information

Why use Ideal Postcodes with WooCommerce?

  • Speed up the Checkout Process. Reduce the amount of typing required during checkout. Customers can search for and select their address instead of entering every address field manually.
  • Increase Deliverability. Help reduce spelling mistakes, formatting errors and incorrectly entered addresses before an order is submitted.
  • Ensure Data Quality. Capture consistent address information using authoritative UK address data from Royal Mail PAF®.

Other Ideal Postcodes Integrations

Ideal Postcodes also provides integrations and setup guides for other WordPress forms:

  • Gravity Forms Address Validation See our guide
  • Contact Form 7 Address Validation See our guide
  • JetFormbuilder Address Validation See our guide
  • Ninja Forms Address Validation See our guide
  • Formidable Forms Address Validation See our guide
  • Forminator Address Validation See our guide
  • Fluent Forms Address Validation See our guide

plugins.name: Fetchify
plugins.author: Fetchify
plugins.short_description: This plugin adds global address auto-complete functionality to the address forms on the front-end in WooCommerce.
plugins.description:
This plugin can be configured to provide up to 4 different data validation products. It replaces our previous plugins Crafty Clicks Address Auto-Complete and Crafty Clicks Postcode Lookup.

Address Auto-Complete

Adds address auto-fill, lookup and validation to address forms on the front-end in WooCommerce for over 240 countries.

The checkout experience becomes faster and easier as a customer no longer has to type out their full address. The smart predictive search helps speed up form filling and boosts usability. Every address is verified at the point of entry. Problems due to incorrect or badly typed address data are drastically reduced.

Postcode Lookup

The defacto solution for address capture and validation in the UK. Enter any UK postcode in the search field, click the search button and the drop down will show all the relevant address results for that postcode. Select the required address and the form will immediately be populated with accurate information.

Phone Validation

Verifies all number types and formats including mobile, international and landline numbers in every country/territory worldwide. Corrects and re-formats common mistakes within forms to ensure data quality.

Email Validation

Email Validation provides real-time validation of any email address. Invalid format emails are declined immediately while valid emails are checked to ensure they link to an active provider. The API verifies username and domain elements of the email address.

Customer Satisfaction & Conversions

Easier and faster checkout saves your customers’ time, improves conversions and builds loyalty.

Data Quality

User input is validated in real time and your customer database is populated with fully verified addresses, phone numbers and email addresses. Address verification can reduce failed deliveries by up to 50%.

WPML Compatibility

This plugin is compatible with WPML to make your checkout multilingual. To find out more about WPML go to https://wpml.org/

Getting Started

In order to use this service, you will need to sign up for an account. You will then receive an access token which will give you access to our service. You need to insert this access token in the configuration options. We offer 30 free searches for testing purposes, but in order to use this plugin on a live site, you must have a paid account with us.

Automatic Updates

Our service is split into 3 parts:

  1. An API server that delivers the data
  2. A JS library that can retrieve the data, and generate a basic UI, regardless of platform
  3. WooCommerce specific JS files (located in clicktoaddress-auto-complete/frontend/js and clicktoaddress-auto-complete/admin/js)

The JS library is located on our CDN to ensure that you will automatically receive any updates. If there’s an update to the API and changes to the JS library are required in order for the plugin to function correctly, you will not have to worry about updating it yourself.

plugins.name: Postcode.eu Address Validation
plugins.author: Postcode.nl B.V.
plugins.short_description: Address autocomplete and validation using the Postcode.eu API. Supports both Dutch and international addresses.
plugins.description:
Postcode.eu Address validation provides address autocomplete and validation with an easy to implement API. The API offers addresses from several European countries, and more countries are constantly being added. We only work with official sources such as postal companies and governments to ensure high quality and accurate data that is up to date.

The Postcode.eu Address Validation plugin uses the Dutch Postcode API and International Address API to streamline the checkout process. By offering autocomplete suggestions for both Dutch and international addresses, it simplifies address input for customers. This functionality helps improve the accuracy of deliveries, reduce return rates due to incorrect addresses, and increase overall customer satisfaction. The result is a more efficient e-commerce operation with a higher conversion rate.

Features

  • Address Autocompletion: This feature drastically reduces the time and effort required to enter addresses, offering autofill suggestions as your customer types, applicable for both Dutch and international addresses.
  • Flexible Dutch Address Completion: Choose to autocomplete Dutch addresses based on postcode and house number, or utilize the single field input feature for an even smoother process.
  • Europe-Wide Coverage: Enjoy access to all supported countries within Europe with a single subscription, expanding the reach of your e-commerce business. View a full list of supported countries here.
  • Data Accuracy: Our plugin draws on official, up-to-date sources such as national cadastre and postal companies, ensuring all address data is precise and accurate.
  • Risk-Free Testing: Try out our API for free and without obligations, enabling you to see firsthand the benefits it can bring to your WooCommerce platform.
  • Typo Recognition: The plugin uses smart technology to detect and correct spelling errors, preventing wrong entries from being saved in your system.
  • Formatted Address Output: Choose to display an easy-to-read address for your customers, offering a clear and streamlined look instead of the standard address fields.
  • Manual Input Option: Gives customers the freedom to bypass autocomplete and manually enter their address if they prefer, ensuring the checkout process is tailored to everyone’s comfort level.
  • Privacy Protection: There are no hidden tracking elements and your data is never resold.
  • Regular Updates: Our system stays current with regular updates to supported countries, ensuring your business remains global without any extra effort.

Account and Pricing

To use the Postcode.eu Address Validation plugin, a separate account is required. Register your account at account.postcode.eu. You can test our service for free. After testing and implementing, you indicate that the subscription can start and you make the choice for a subscription. For information on pricing, visit our website.

Third-Party Service Usage

This plugin relies on the Postcode.eu API, a third-party service, for address autocompletion and validation. The use of this service is essential for the plugin’s functionality, enabling it to provide accurate address suggestions and validations across multiple countries using official postal data.

  • Terms and Conditions
  • Privacy policy

API Usage Context

  • The service is used during the checkout process to offer address autocompletion suggestions to the user.
  • The plugin communicates with the Postcode.eu API servers to retrieve address data based on the input provided by the user.
  • A valid Postcode.eu account is required to access the API services.

For more details on the Postcode.eu API and how to obtain an account, please visit Postcode.eu.

plugins.name: Shipping Simulator for WooCommerce
plugins.author: Link Nacional
plugins.short_description: Calculate shipping on product and cart pages, with free shipping rules, progress bar and address autofill for WooCommerce.
plugins.description:
Shipping Simulator for WooCommerce brings the shipping calculator to your customers while they are still browsing: directly on the product page and on the cart page. Instead of waiting until checkout, customers enter their postcode (CEP) and instantly see the available shipping methods, price and estimated delivery time.

The plugin also helps increase your average order value with free shipping rules — by minimum cart amount or per product — and a configurable free-shipping progress bar that shows the customer how much is left to unlock free shipping. Results are cached and the last postcode is remembered, so repeated lookups are fast.

Calculator features

  • Calculate shipping directly from the product page
  • Calculate shipping from the cart page
  • Free shipping by minimum amount and by product
  • Visual customization: colors, borders, icons and position of the fields

Legacy simulator features

  • Calculate shipping without having to choose variations (Check it on the plugin settings page)
  • Automatically fills in and updates the customer’s address (Check it on the plugin settings page)
  • Uses the same postcode field, button and results list described below
  • If you are using some page builder, use the shortcode [wc_shipping_simulator]

PRO version

Upgrade to Shipping Simulator for WooCommerce PRO for advanced features:

  • CEP validation popup that asks visitors to confirm delivery availability, with WhatsApp contact when delivery isn’t available
  • Hide the address fields automatically when the customer selects local pickup
  • Delivery time system: business days and hours, delivery time slots and order deadline tracking

Calculator fields

The calculator is deliberately short: the customer only types the postcode and gets the shipping options right away.

  • Postcode / CEP (postcode): the only address field on the calculator. It is required, can be typed as text or number, and its placeholder is configurable. Brazilian stores can also look the address up automatically from it.
  • Calculate shipping (submit button): triggers the lookup. Its label is configurable, and the field and the button can be repositioned (inline, stacked or floating over the product image).
  • Shipping results (results list): one line per shipping method, with the method name, the price and the estimated delivery time. It is filled by AJAX, without reloading the page.
  • Free shipping progress bar: shows how much is left to unlock free shipping, on the cart, and the message shown when the customer gets there. Its texts, colors and values are configurable.
  • Country, State and City (native fields, not shown for Brazil): Brazilian stores see only the postcode field and get the address filled in automatically. Stores in other countries keep WooCommerce’s default calculator with all address fields.

Settings

Access your admin panel and open WooCommerce > Settings > Calculadora de frete to configure the new shipping calculator, free shipping and progress bar options. The previous simulator settings still exist and are now available as WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Simulador de Frete (Legado).

Contributions

For bugs, suggestions or contributions, open an issue in our GitHub Repository or create a topic in the WordPress Plugin Forum.

Donations

plugins.name: Campos Checkout Brasileiro para WooCommerce
plugins.author: Link Nacional
plugins.short_description: Brazilian checkout fields: CPF/CNPJ, address number, neighborhood and phone, with automatic CEP address pre-filling and much more for WooCommerce.
plugins.description:
Complete Brazilian checkout fields designed specifically for Brazilian Market on WooCommerce stores in Brazil, making it easier and significantly improving the data entry flow on the checkout pages.

This version includes full compatibility with Shortcodes and Gutenberg themes, allowing you to use the Brazilian checkout fields anywhere on your site with maximum flexibility.

This WordPress plugin ensures faster address verification and cleaner form management, leading to a better user experience and fewer abandoned carts.

Note: The shipping calculator features have moved to a dedicated plugin: Shipping Simulator for WooCommerce.

🚀 Full and Free Brazilian Checkout

We have expanded the plugin capabilities to offer a full checkout solution for the Brazilian Market on WooCommerce, managing Custom Checkout Fields essential for Brazilian logistics and fiscal invoicing. Every field is listed — with its meta key and what it does — in the Checkout fields section below.

✅ ERP & “Brazilian Market” Compatibility

This is a major update for store owners who need to issue invoices (Nota Fiscal). The plugin is now fully compatible with other payment’s plugin for the data standards used by the Brazilian Market on WooCommerce plugin by Claudio Sanches.

Why is this important?
1. Bling & ERP Integration: CPF, CNPJ and address data are saved with the standard meta keys (the same ones listed below), so this plugin is fully compatible with Bling, Tiny and other ERPs that integrate with WooCommerce. You can issue invoices (NFe) without data errors.
2. No double data entry: the same value feeds the checkout, the order, the customer profile and the invoice app.

Key Features & Improvements:

On the Checkout Page:

  • Automatic Address Lookup: Fills in street, neighborhood, city and state as soon as the customer enters a valid CEP.
  • Input Validation: Checks CPF/CNPJ digits and applies input masks, so a wrong number is caught before the order is placed.
  • Dynamic Field Hiding: Hides the fields that do not apply to the customer — company data for individuals, CPF and RG for companies — and gives the typed value back when the field returns.
  • Person Type Selector: In the block checkout the customer can switch between “Person” (Pessoa Física) and “Company” (Pessoa Jurídica); in the classic checkout the type follows the document that was typed.

Additional Features:

  • The plugin is fully customizable via action and filter hooks for advanced users.

More details can be found in the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ).

Checkout fields

Below is every field the plugin adds or manages, on the billing and shipping address forms (classic checkout, block checkout, the account’s edit-address page and the order admin screen):

  • CPF/CNPJ (billing_document): a single document field with mask and validation. It reads the number of digits to tell individuals (CPF, 11 digits) from companies (CNPJ, 14 digits) — and that choice drives the rest of the form.
  • Person type (billing_persontype): hidden field that stores the type worked out from the document, so other plugins and ERPs read “individual” or “company” the way they expect.
  • CPF (billing_cpf) and CNPJ (billing_cnpj): hidden companions that receive the same value as the document, for invoice (NF-e) plugins and ERPs that look for these keys.
  • Company (billing_company): shown for companies. Its behavior is configurable — Dynamic, Optional, Required or Disabled.
  • State registration / Inscrição Estadual (billing_ie): shown for companies, with an “Isento” (exempt) checkbox. Required when enabled.
  • Municipal registration / Inscrição Municipal (billing_im): shown for companies and required for them. No “Isento” option, because the municipal registration is what identifies the business for service invoices.
  • RG (billing_rg): shown for individuals only, next to the CPF, and hidden for companies. Optional by default. Saved with the same key used by invoice apps, so the value is already there when you issue the nota fiscal.
  • Number (billing_number): the street number, mandatory and usually missing from standard WooCommerce forms. It comes with a “Sem Número” (no number) checkbox that fills the field for addresses without a number.
  • Neighborhood / Bairro (billing_neighborhood): mandatory neighborhood field, placed right after the address.
  • Complement (billing_address_2): the native WooCommerce complement, renamed and repositioned.
  • Phone (billing_phone): phone field with mask and country code (DDI). Four modes: full phone, cellphone only, landline only or disabled. Optional validation of the number (including the area code).
  • Cellphone (billing_cellphone): optional separate cellphone field, filled in alongside the phone, and a hidden mirror for gateways that expect it.
  • Birthdate (billing_birthdate): optional date field, with an option to make it required.
  • Gender (billing_gender): optional dropdown (Male, Female, Non-binary, Other, Prefer not to say).
  • Postcode / CEP (billing_postcode): can be highlighted at the top of the form, with a confirmation checkbox and automatic address lookup.
  • Country, State and City (billing_country, billing_state, billing_city): the native WooCommerce fields, kept in place and repositioned so the Brazilian order of the address makes sense.

Every field above can be turned on or off in WooCommerce > Settings > Campos Brasileiros, together with its required/optional rule.

plugins.author: FullStack-ing
plugins.short_description: Configure COD restrictions and extra fees for WooCommerce Classic Checkout and Cart & Checkout Blocks.
plugins.description:
Smart COD for WooCommerce extends the WooCommerce Cash on Delivery (COD) Gateway with an optional extra fee and restrictions based on customer conditions such as location and selected shipping method.

Supports both Classic Checkout and WooCommerce Cart & Checkout Blocks (WooCommerce 9.9+ for Blocks). The same COD restrictions and extra fees apply to both checkout types.

Whether you’re managing a small shop or a large e-commerce business, this plugin helps you fine-tune your Cash on Delivery service to cater to a wide range of scenarios and requirements.

A common challenge faced by WooCommerce store owners is the inability to apply an extra fee for the Cash on Delivery (COD) payment method. This is a critical feature for many e-commerce shops, as charging an additional fee for COD is a standard practice.
The plugin also offers configurable restrictions so merchants can decide when COD is available.

A separate Smart COD PRO plugin is available outside the WordPress.org directory. It adds advance-payment COD, multiple conditional extra fees (including country, shipping-zone and shipping-method pricing, cart-amount thresholds and order-pay handling), CSV restriction imports, and cart amount, product quantity, customer-role, stock, backorder and coupon rules. These features are part of the separate PRO plugin, not locked options in this Free plugin.

Restrictions

Each restriction can be easily toggled between Enable and Disable. When set to Enable, the restriction will allow the Cash on Delivery (COD) payment option only for the specified selections. On the other hand, when set to Disable, the restriction will disable the COD option for the specified selections, making it unavailable for them.

  • Shipping Zone
  • Shipping Method inside Shipping Zone
  • Country
  • State
  • Postal Code (Supports Ranges)
  • City
  • User Role
  • Products in cart (Supports Variations)
  • Categories of the products in cart
  • Shipping Class

You can define an informational message to display before the payment methods, when the COD method is not available for a customer.
You can define different messages per restrict reason.

Extra Fees

You can configure a standard extra fee and a separate fee for local pickup.

You can use a fixed price or a percentage of the customer’s cart amount.
You also have a nice rounding option.
You can enable tax for this fee.

Developer-Friendly

The plugin integrates seamlessly with WooCommerce and uses a clean, object-oriented codebase. It also provides the following filters for easy customization:

  • wc_smart_cod_fee: Alter the extra fee.
  • wc_smart_cod_available: Alter the current COD restriction.
  • wc_smart_cod_fee_title: Change the COD fee title.

Since the plugin extends the existing WooCommerce Cash on Delivery Gateway, there’s no need to enable or disable gateways manually.

External services

COD Protection and order-history sharing are optional and off by default in Free and PRO. Enabling the sharing setting in Cash on Delivery settings registers the installation with api.woosmartcod.com and permits the collection described below. Collection includes future physical COD creation snapshots and subsequent outcomes in signed background batches, without requiring tracking or a 24-hour wait. The existing filtered cancellation relay still sends eligible historical and future cancellation evidence and a capped prior-completed tracked COD count for the same shopper at that shop. An existing enabled sharing setting applies to this collection after updating, without another activation step or expansion notice; disabled settings remain disabled. Registration includes a generated installation identifier, shop domain, operating country and public signing key. Events include pseudonymized customer/location identifiers, a non-reversible order reference, timestamps, totals/currency, shipping method, item count, guest/registered status and courier/tracking where available. The service validates signed submissions, deduplicates events and applies an additional secret-keyed transformation to identity tokens. Data supports same-store COD protection and, subject to server-side eligibility review, cross-store machine-learning training; collection does not activate live ML scoring. No individual shop could perform that cross-shop processing locally.

When COD Protection is enabled and checkout contains an email address or telephone number, the plugin sends locally generated SHA-256 identity tokens, the installation identifier and operating country to the COD Protection endpoint. Raw email and telephone values are not sent. The service checks only eligible events belonging to that same installation and returns only an allow/disable decision with a decision reference and policy metadata, not customer-history counts. The service records aggregate decision statistics and pseudonymized supporting evidence for denials, rather than storing every raw checkout lookup request. A timeout, invalid response or unavailable service leaves Cash on Delivery available. Turning the option off stops future collection, transmission and checkout lookups. The plugin does not call courier APIs.

Service information: cancelled COD service privacy details, Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy.

COD Protection, successful history and order lifecycle

Classic shortcode checkout remains supported. Cart and Checkout Blocks are also supported on WooCommerce 9.9 or newer through the native Store API and Blocks extension APIs. The same COD rules, fees and optional order-lifecycle collection apply to both checkouts. Third-party gateways and checkout fields require their own Blocks support.

Changes in this release: collection expands from filtered cancellation evidence to prospective physical COD creation and outcome events. The successful-history allowance adds context so earlier cancellations are not considered in isolation. This prepares representative data for cross-store machine-learning training; receiving data does not automatically activate ML scoring at checkout.

New lifecycle events do NOT require tracking or a 24-hour wait. A new physical COD order created and cancelled within minutes is still recorded whenever the sharing setting is enabled. Other payment methods, virtual-only orders and deposit-child orders are excluded. Existing historical cancellations retain their filtered relay: this release does not import all past creations or completed orders.

Collection and COD restriction are different. Not every collected cancellation is a qualifying negative match. The existing shipment/fulfilment checks remain: tracking, a prior physical-order completed status or a shipped/fulfilled transition. The lower-confidence untracked fallback applies only without a recognized tracking integration, after at least 24 hours between creation and cancellation, with a fulfilment-stage source status when supplied. Tracking AND 24 hours are not universal joint requirements. A cancellation by itself is not proof of refusal or non-delivery.

Optional, off by default, and identical in Free and PRO. Protection checks only this installation. When the existing sharing setting is enabled, the plugin sends future physical COD creation snapshots and later status/outcome changes (including completed, cancelled, refunded and reopened orders) to api.woosmartcod.com in signed background batches. Creation snapshots include pseudonymized email/telephone and postcode identifiers, order reference, timing, totals/currency, shipping method, item count and guest/registered status. Courier names and tracking codes are included where available. Raw customer email, telephone and names are not sent. Data is used for COD protection and, subject to server-side eligibility review, cross-store machine-learning training.

There is one sharing setting. After updating, stores that already enabled sharing also collect future physical COD creation snapshots and subsequent outcomes, without a separate activation or upgrade notice. Stores with sharing disabled remain disabled. Switching sharing off stops future capture, transmission and checkout checks. Historical cancellations keep their existing compatibility relay. Old orders first observed after the update or activation are marked as late observations, not invented checkout snapshots.

The configurable successful-history allowance uses only directly matching email or telephone in this store and affects only the history-based restriction. Default minimum rate: 100%, preserving the existing history restriction unless the merchant chooses a lower rate (50% to 100%). Nine known successful orders and one qualifying dispatched-then-cancelled order meet 90%. Pending orders do not count. WooCommerce completed status is merchant-reported, not automatically courier-confirmed. New completion rows and cumulative historical snapshots are not summed: the service uses a conservative maximum to avoid counting the same deliveries twice. Exact individually imported historical success coverage may therefore be incomplete.

Checkout calls contain hashed identifiers, not raw identity values. The service records aggregate operational counts and pseudonymized evidence for actual denials. This is distinct from storing every raw lookup request. Transport/service errors fail open. More details: https://woosmartcod.com/cancelled-cod-data-sharing/

plugins.name: Geo Controller – Geolocation & Geotargeting
plugins.author: INFINITUM FORM
plugins.short_description: WordPress geolocation and geotargeting with IP lookup, geo redirects, dynamic content, WooCommerce localization and visitor blocking.
plugins.description:
Geo Controller is a WordPress geolocation and geotargeting plugin that uses IP location data to personalize website content, redirect visitors by country or region, localize WooCommerce, and control geographic access. It combines location-based shortcodes, conditional content, geo redirects, country flags, Google Maps, Geo Defender, and developer APIs in one plugin.

Previously known as CF Geo Plugin, Geo Controller continues the development of the original WordPress geolocation plugin under its new name. Existing users can continue using supported shortcodes, integrations, and location-based functionality without switching to a different plugin.

WordPress IP Geolocation

Geo Controller resolves a visitor’s IP address through the Geo Controller API and makes the available location data accessible in WordPress. Depending on the lookup response and enabled options, this can include country, region, city, postcode, coordinates, timezone, language, currency, ISP, hostname, proxy, TOR, and device information.

  • IPv4 and IPv6 lookup support
  • Trusted proxy and Cloudflare-aware IP detection
  • Configurable SSL, proxy, cache, and API transport settings
  • Default values when requested data is unavailable
  • Optional DNS, ISP, currency, and device-related data

IP geolocation is approximate. VPNs, proxies, mobile networks, shared connections, CDN configuration, and database accuracy can affect results. Review data sources and accuracy and IP detection guidance before using location data for important decisions.

Geotargeting and Dynamic Content

Use WordPress shortcodes to display visitor data or conditionally show content by country, region, city, continent, postcode, EU status, VAT status, proxy, TOR, or device type. Geo Banner rules provide another way to target text, media, and other WordPress content.

Common examples:

[cfgeo return="country"]
[cfgeo return="city" default="Your Default Text"]
[cfgeo include="US,GB,DE"]Content for selected countries.[/cfgeo]
[in_eu]Content for EU visitors.[/in_eu]

Nested shortcodes remain available in conditional content where the surrounding WordPress content area processes shortcodes. Optional Simple Shortcodes, such as [cfgeo_city], must be enabled in Geo Controller settings. See the shortcode reference for supported attributes and return values.

Location-specific HTML can be affected by full-page caching when one cached response is shared between visitors. Follow the dynamic content and caching guidance and test every rule with a safe fallback.

Common Geolocation Use Cases

Geo Controller can be used to create location-aware WordPress experiences without building a separate geolocation system.

  • Display different content, messages, banners, or affiliate links based on visitor location.
  • Redirect visitors to country-specific pages, regional websites, or localized content.
  • Show local contact information, phone numbers, addresses, and Google Maps.
  • Customize WooCommerce payment options and currency information by visitor location.
  • Restrict access from selected countries, IP addresses, proxies, or TOR networks.
  • Provide location-based information to custom themes, plugins, forms, and integrations.

These features can be combined using shortcodes, conditional content, WordPress integrations, and developer APIs. Availability depends on configuration and, for selected features, the active license.

Geo Redirects and Geographic SEO Redirection

Create ordered geographic rules for pages, posts, custom post types, or site-wide destinations. Rules can evaluate supported country, region, city, and postcode values, with exclusions, bot handling, referrer controls, and CSV import/export tools.

Available response codes are 301, 302, 303, 307, 308, and 404. Choose the response that matches the intended behavior: permanent redirects should not be used while destinations are still being tested, and 404 returns a not-found response rather than redirecting the visitor.

Redirects do not guarantee search-engine results or legal compliance. Avoid redirect loops, keep destinations crawlable where appropriate, and test caching, canonical URLs, language settings, and bot behavior before production use.

WooCommerce Geolocation, Currency and Payments

The included WooCommerce integration can use Geo Controller location data to support:

  • Customer geolocation and location data saved with orders
  • Country-based payment gateway visibility
  • Local currency information and currency conversion
  • EU and VAT-aware content
  • Classic Checkout, Checkout Blocks, Store API, and HPOS workflows

Some WooCommerce controls and service-backed data require an eligible active license. Availability is shown in the plugin settings. Currency results are informational and may not match the final rate used by a payment provider, bank, tax service, or accounting system.

Geo Defender and Visitor Access Control

Geo Defender can restrict access using configured geographic and IP rules, with support for TOR, proxy, and spam-related signals where available. Administrators can configure a response, allow trusted addresses, receive notifications, and use the existing recovery mechanism if a rule blocks administrative access.

Geolocation and reputation signals can be incomplete or incorrect. Geo Defender is an access-control aid, not a replacement for authentication, a firewall, malware protection, or professional security and compliance review. Test rules carefully before enabling them on a production site.

Google Maps, Country Flags and Geographic Metadata

Enable [cfgeo_map] to display a single-point Google Map for a detected or specified location. A valid Google Maps API key is required.

[cfgeo_map longitude="-74.0059" latitude="40.7128" zoom="15" title="My Company Name"]
    <h3>My Company Name</h3>
    <p>No Name Street 35, New York, USA</p>
    <p>We have what you need</p>
[/cfgeo_map]

Geo tags can add configured geographic metadata to selected public content. Country flags are available through [cfgeo_flag], including custom country, size, class, ID, inline CSS, and include/exclude options.

Examples:

[cfgeo_flag]
[cfgeo_flag country="ca" size="32px"]

Read the Google Maps shortcode documentation before enabling map output. Google Maps is a separate external service with its own account, billing, terms, and privacy behavior.

Integrations and Developer Features

The plugin contains dedicated integration code for WooCommerce, Elementor, Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, BuddyBoss Platform, WooPlatnica, and Yoast SEO. It also includes Cloudflare-aware IP handling and settings intended for common caching configurations. Compatibility still depends on the active theme, plugin versions, cache/CDN behavior, and site configuration.

Developers can use:

  • CFGP_U::api() for the current structured geodata array
  • CFGP_U::api('country_code') for a single available field
  • CFGP_API::lookup() for an explicit advanced lookup
  • window.cfgeo when the plugin’s JavaScript output is enabled
  • Native WordPress do_shortcode() in templates that intentionally render shortcode content
  • The optional public REST lookup feature when the required license level is active

Always validate returned keys and provide fallbacks because not every lookup returns every field.

Free and Licensed Features

The plugin can be installed and used without a paid license. The standard Geo Controller API allowance is up to 500 lookups per day. An active paid license provides unlimited lookups during its license period, and some service-backed features are enabled according to license level.

License-dependent controls can include automatic spam-IP checks, selected WooCommerce payment controls, and the public REST lookup service. The admin interface indicates whether a setting requires a license. Current license plans, available features, and site limits are listed on the pricing page.

Geo Controller depends on an external API service for IP lookup data. Review the Privacy Policy and privacy, consent, and compliance documentation to decide how the service fits your site’s disclosures and legal obligations.

Plugin Links

  • Geo Controller Website
  • Documentation
  • Contact & Support
  • Terms and Conditions
  • Privacy Policy

External Services and Privacy

Geo Controller sends IP lookup requests to the Geo Controller API. Optional Google Maps output uses Google Maps separately when configured. Site owners are responsible for evaluating these services, providing appropriate notices or consent, and meeting applicable legal requirements.

Review the Privacy Policy, Terms and Conditions, and privacy documentation before deployment.

plugins.name: AutoPostcode
plugins.author: creativemarketingltd
plugins.short_description: This plugin adds UK address postcode lookup functionality on the checkout page of your website and is exclusively designed for WooCommerce.
plugins.description:
Our plugin allows your website visitors to experience a faster checkout by simply entering their postcode and selecting their address from a dropwdown list.

Address postcode lookup

Adds an address dropdown list upon postcode entry on your WooCommerce checkout page.

AutoPostcode helps your users to experience a smoother and faster checkout by simply entering their postcode and selecting their address. This can help to improve your website conversion rate, reduce abandoned cart and also minimise shipping errors.

Improve Conversion Rates

The faster it is for a user to checkout, the more conversions you can receive. This plugin speeds your checkout.

Reduce Shipping Errors

By enabling the users to select an address from a pre-defined address list reduces shipping errors as there is minimal chance of typos and incorrectly entered addresses.

How to Use

Simply create an account on app.autopostcode.com and generate your secret key. Enter the key into your Auto Postcode Plugin settings. That’s it.

Automatic Updates

Our plugin is regularly updated to enhance the functionality, user experience and security features. The plugin can be automatically updated by enabling “Auto-Updates”.

plugins.name: WC – APG City
plugins.author: Art Project Group
plugins.short_description: Adds to WooCommerce an automatic city name generated from the postcode.
plugins.description:
WC – APG City adds to your WooCommerce store a new automatic city field generated from the postcode via the GeoNames API or the Google Maps API.

Features

  • Fully compatible with the Checkout block in the WordPress block editor.
  • Includes a local GeoNames database that is downloaded and updated monthly to improve performance and reduce external API queries.
  • You can choose between the GeoNames API and the Google Maps API.
  • You must add your own Google Maps API Key or GeoNames username.
  • Your API credentials are never sent to the browser: every lookup is made by the server.
  • You can customize the default text of the select field.
  • You can customize the text of the option used to switch to a text field.
  • You can block modifications to the city and province (state) fields.
  • You can customize the background color of the locked fields.
  • If the postcode is shared by more than one city, the customer can select the correct city name from the list returned by GeoNames or Google Maps.
  • If the city is not in the list or cannot be found in either API, the customer can manually enter their city name.
  • It also selects the province (state), as long as the name matches the one obtained from GeoNames or Google Maps.

Translations

  • English: by Art Project Group (default language).
  • Spanish: by Art Project Group.

More information

You can learn more about WC – APG City on our official website, and follow the development on GitHub.

Thanks

Thanks to everyone who uses the plugin, helps improve it, makes a donation or encourages us with their comments.

If you find this plugin useful, you can support its development with a small donation.

External Services

  1. To the GeoNames services, to download and update, on a monthly basis, the full local database of cities and postcodes, as well as to perform queries to its API when there is no information in the local database.

    • It sends the country and the postcode.
    • More information: https://www.geonames.org/export/

  2. To the Google Maps API, to obtain the city and state/province name from the postcode and country when this option is selected in the plugin settings.

    • It sends the country and the postcode.
    • More information: https://policies.google.com/privacy

plugins.name: Kybernaut IČO DIČ
plugins.author: Karolina Vyskocilova
plugins.short_description: Adds Company & VAT numbers (IČO & DIČ & IČ DPH) to WooCommerce billing fields and verifies if data are correct.
plugins.description:
Adds Company & VAT numbers (IČO & DIČ & IČ DPH) to WooCommerce billing fields and verifies if data are correct. Verification is based either on ARES and VIES database or only on mathematics. When billing to Czech republic, you can autofill fields Company, VAT number, Address, City, and Postcode based on IČO.

The plugin doesn’t support block checkout. [Use shortcode checkout instead or “Classic checkout block”.] (https://kybernaut.cz/clanky/jak-vratit-starou-woocommerce-pokladnu-misto-noveho-bloku/)

Supports both PHP 7.3+ (soon to be abandoned) & PHP 8.0+.

Main functionality

  • for CZ as billing country
    • ARES and VIES verification (or mathematically verifies IČO and DIČ)
    • ARES autofill (fields Company, VAT number, Address, City, and Postcode) based on IČO
  • for SK as billing country
    • VIES DIČ validation (or just validate the format of values)
  • for EU countries as billing country
    • VIES DIČ validation
  • VAT exempt feature
  • adds fields to IČO & DIČ & IČ DPH WooCommerce frontend: Checkout and My Account page
  • allows edits from administration (backend):
    • Users -> Joe Doe (Edit) -> Billing address of the customer
    • E-shop-WooCommerce -> Orders-> Order (show(edit)) -> Billing Information (edit)
  • Enable toggle switch to show/hide input fields (“Buying as a company?”)
  • Move Country field above the “Buying as a company?” toggle
  • Option to allow on order if if ARES or VIES check fails for technical reasons – an alert will be shown in the admin mail and order details

Compatibility

  • Kybernaut Mailstep by Karolína Vyskočilová
  • WooCommerce SuperFaktura by 2day.sk & Webikon
  • WooCommerce PDF Invoices & Packing Slips for WooCommerce by WP Overnight
  • WooCommerce PDF Invoices and Packing Slips for WooCommerce PRO by Acowebs
  • WooCommerce Sequential Order Numbers by SkyVerge
  • Woo Checkout Field Editor Pro by ThemeHigh
  • Fluid Checkout for WooCommerce – Lite by Fluid Checkout – only partial support
  • Woo iDoklad, Woo Doprava, Woo GoPay etc. by Toret (affiliate link)

Requirements

  • SoapClient PHP library for VIES validation (ask your hosting)

Credits

  • 10up and their WordPress.org Plugin Deploy and WordPress.org Plugin Readme/Assets Update Github Actions
  • ibericode/vat

If you want to help, join the Github.

plugins.name: Postcode Checkout – Address Validation | WooCommerce
plugins.author: CodeBrain BV
plugins.short_description: 📦 Validate Customer Addresses in WooCommerce
plugins.description:
Using WooCommerce for WordPress and want to make sure your customers enter valid, deliverable addresses? This plugin does the job perfectly!
Save time, reduce failed deliveries, and make checkout smoother by validating addresses in real time through trusted postcode databases.

Features

✅ Easy to use – Quick setup and seamless integration with WooCommerce.
✅ Accurate address validation – Verify customer data instantly using reliable postcode sources such as Postcode EU, Pro6PP, Postcode API, Nederland Postcode API and Postcode Connect.
✅ Dutch & international support – Works with national (The Netherlands) and international addresses across: The Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Luxembourg, Austria, Switzerland, France, United Kingdom, Spain, Denmark, Norway, Finland, and Sweden.
✅ Fully configurable – Adjust validation rules and settings to match your checkout’s workflow.
✅ Fully functional test environment available – Try it risk-free before choosing your databroker and see how much time you save!

Requirements

⚙️ You can create a free Postcode Checkout account and fully test the plugin before choosing your databroker.
⚙️ This plugin requires an Postcode Checkout license to perform real address validation and autocompletion. Licenses can be puchased at: https://www.postcode-checkout.nl/en/pricing
⚙️ This plugin requires an active postcode database account from one of our supported databrokers (i.e. Postcode EU, Pro6PP, Postcode API, Nederland Postcode API and Postcode Connect)

Postcode EU
Postcode API
Pro6PP
Nederland Postcode API
Postcode Connect

External services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

  1. Postcode Checkout by CodeBrain BV

    • Service URL: Postcode Checkout dashboard
    • Privacy policy: Privacy Policy
    • Terms: Terms and Conditions
    • Purpose: validates the merchant API key and performs international address lookup (suggestions and details) and national addresses. Additionally retrieves the supported countries in case of international Postcode EU or Pro6PP.
    • When requests are sent: when an administrator saves or validates the plugin API key, and when a visitor uses address validation or autocomplete in a Contact Form 7 form where this plugin is enabled.
    • Data sent: the API key in the Authorization header, the site URL in the Referer header, a User-Agent string containing the plugin name and author, and lookup data such as country, search query, postcode, house number, house number addition, selected address identifier, and autocomplete session identifier where applicable.

plugins.name: Eventward
plugins.author: OmnisWP
plugins.short_description: The complete events calendar, free: recurring events, six views, maps, tickets and RSVP with no platform fee. No Pro version, nothing locked.
plugins.description:
Eventward is a complete events calendar for WordPress, and all of it is free. Recurring events, six calendar views, maps, venues, organizers, tickets and RSVP come in one plugin. There is no Pro version, no add-on store, no licence key and no feature held back for a paid tier.

It is built for sites that need to stay fast and correct: event dates live in their own indexed table, repeating schedules are expanded by a real iCalendar engine, and paid tickets go straight to your own Stripe account with no fee from us.

What makes Eventward different

  • Everything is in the free plugin. Recurring events, every view, maps, filters, tickets and RSVP. Most event plugins sell these as add-ons; here there is nothing to upgrade to.
  • Built on a proper date index. Each event date is stored as a row in one small indexed table, instead of being searched out of post meta. Month, week and list views stay quick as a calendar grows into thousands of dates, and every event keeps its real post ID, so other plugins and page builder loops work with it normally.
  • Recurring events that get the details right. Schedules follow the iCalendar standard (RRULE), with skipped and extra dates. Each event has its own timezone, and a 7pm weekly event stays at 7pm when the clocks change.
  • Tickets with no platform fee. Free tickets work as an RSVP. Paid tickets use Stripe Checkout on your own Stripe account: buyers pay you directly and you only pay Stripe’s standard processing fees.
  • Search engine friendly by design. Every event page carries schema.org Event data for Google. Calendar navigation cannot turn into an endless crawl: dated calendar pages are noindex, navigation links are nofollow and empty far-future months return 404.
  • An easy move from The Events Calendar. A built-in importer copies your events, venues, organizers, categories and ticket types across without changing anything in The Events Calendar. Event, venue, organizer, month and day URLs follow the same patterns, and an optional setting lets existing [tribe_events] shortcodes keep working, so links and pages survive the switch.

Calendar and views

  • Six views: month, week, list, photo, map and day, as a block you can place anywhere, plus ready-made templates for block themes. Classic themes are supported too.
  • Search and filters by keyword, category, venue and organizer, applied in place without reloading the page.
  • Mobile friendly. On small screens the month view becomes an easy-to-read agenda.
  • Category colours. Give each category a colour and show it as a line before each event or as the event’s background in the month and week views.
  • Your choice of display. 24-hour or 12-hour times, and full event names in the month view for long titles.
  • Light on your pages. Styles and scripts only load where events are shown, and moving between months and views updates the calendar in place.

Recurring events and time zones

  • Daily, weekly, monthly (“the second Tuesday”, “the last Friday”) and yearly schedules, with intervals, end dates, counts, skipped dates and extra dates.
  • A custom option for anything else the iCalendar standard can describe.
  • A timezone per event, with correct local times across daylight saving changes.
  • Each date of a repeating event has its own page and its own entry in Google’s event data.

Venues, organizers and maps

  • Create venues and organizers inline while editing an event. Each gets its own page listing its upcoming events.
  • Maps without API keys. OpenStreetMap maps for the calendar, venues and events, with clustered pins, bundled with the plugin.
  • Place venues by typing their coordinates, or turn on address lookup (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, off by default) to find them from the address when you save.

Tickets and RSVP

  • Free RSVP and paid tickets, several ticket types per event, with capacity per type and per date.
  • Stripe Checkout in test and live mode. Connect your Stripe account in one click, or paste a restricted API key.
  • Seats are held while a buyer pays and released automatically if they do not finish, so a date does not oversell.
  • Confirmation emails with ticket codes, an attendee list with check-in, CSV export, one-click refunds and resending confirmations.
  • Your own booking questions on each ticket type (short or long text, dropdown, yes-or-no tick box, phone number), answered once per ticket, with answers on the attendee list, in the CSV and in the emails. Logged-in visitors find their name and email already filled in, which suits membership sites.
  • Reports: bookings, check-ins, no-shows and takings by month, by date and by ticket type for any period, with capacity filled per date and a CSV export for your annual figures.
  • An optional Stripe webhook for instant confirmations. Without it, payments are still confirmed when buyers return and by a background check.
  • Bookings are included in WordPress’s personal data export and erasure tools.

Themes, blocks and page builders

  • Native blocks and Site Editor templates for block themes.
  • Shortcodes for the calendar, event details, single fields (date, venue, cost and more), tickets and maps, for Bricks, Divi, Elementor and other builders.
  • A sortable “next date” field for page builder query loops.

Sharing and SEO

  • schema.org Event data on every event: status, attendance mode, location, organizer, price and availability.
  • Add to calendar links for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook and Microsoft 365, plus subscribable iCal feeds for the whole calendar or any category.
  • Event status for cancelled, postponed, rescheduled and moved online events, shown on the page and sent to Google.

Fair by default

  • No upsells, no admin banners, no ads and no tracking. Every external service Eventward can use is listed below, with what it sends and when.
  • Your data stays yours: deactivating never deletes anything, and uninstalling only removes events if you ask it to.
  • Translation ready.

Eventward is made by OmnisWP, the team behind Siteward.

External services

Eventward works on your own site, except for the services below:

  • OpenStreetMap Nominatim (geocoding). Off by default: nothing is sent until an admin turns on address lookup under Events > Settings > Maps. When on, it turns venue addresses into map locations. Your site contacts https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org when a venue is saved with a new or changed address, when you press “Find on map”, and in an hourly background check that looks up to 10 venues that have never been looked up (for example imported ones). Venues whose coordinates you typed yourself are never looked up. Each request sends the venue’s address (street, city, region, postcode, country), your site’s address (in the User-Agent, as Nominatim’s policy requires) and your site’s language. Nothing about your visitors is sent. You can turn it off again at any time. Usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ Privacy policy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy
  • OpenStreetMap map tiles. Pages that show a map load map images from https://tile.openstreetmap.org in the visitor’s browser (only once the map scrolls into view). The visitor’s IP address and the page address are visible to that server, as with any image. Tile usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ Privacy policy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy You can switch to another tile provider under Events > Settings > Maps.
  • Add to calendar links (Google Calendar, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365) are ordinary links: nothing is sent unless a visitor clicks one.
  • Stripe (payments). Only when you sell paid tickets. Your site talks to https://api.stripe.com to create Stripe Checkout sessions, confirm payments and make refunds. For each checkout your site sends the buyer’s email address, the event title, date and time, the tickets with their prices, an order reference and the addresses of your event page that Stripe returns the buyer to; card details are entered on Stripe’s own page and never touch your site. If you add the optional webhook in your Stripe Dashboard, Stripe also sends payment and refund notices to your site. Stripe terms: https://stripe.com/legal Privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy
  • OmnisWP connection service. Only if you choose “Connect with Stripe” instead of pasting an API key. Stripe’s app login needs a secret held by OmnisWP, so https://omniswp.com/wp-json/omnis-connect/v1 is contacted only when an admin presses “Connect with Stripe” (your site first checks the service is available for that mode), and while connected, to renew the short-lived access token: by a background check every 30 minutes, and on demand if the token has run out when your site next talks to Stripe (for example during a booking). When connecting, the admin’s browser takes the mode (test or live), a one-time challenge and the address of your site’s Payments screen to omniswp.com, and your site then sends the one-time claim code and its matching secret to collect the tokens. When renewing, your site sends the mode and the refresh token. Like any WordPress request, these carry your site’s address in the User-Agent. The service never sees payments or buyer details, and keeps nothing after handing the tokens to your site. Terms: https://omniswp.com/terms/ Privacy policy: https://omniswp.com/privacy-policy/

Third-party libraries

  • Leaflet 1.9.4, BSD 2-Clause licence, https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet (bundled in assets/vendor/leaflet, minified build from the official npm package)
  • Leaflet.markercluster 1.5.3, MIT licence, https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet.markercluster (bundled in assets/vendor/leaflet-markercluster)

plugins.name: Address Lookup field for ACF
plugins.author: Justin Kruit
plugins.short_description: ACF field integration for address lookup providers.
plugins.description:
Address Lookup field for ACF adds an address lookup field type to Advanced Custom Fields. Users can search for addresses directly within the editor, and the field returns structured address data including coordinates.

The plugin uses Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) as the default lookup provider, and supports registering custom providers.

The plugin also includes support for the Photon geocoding provider out of the box. You can choose between Nominatim and Photon, or register your own providers.

Features

  • Live address search — AJAX-powered search as you type, using Select2.
  • Structured data — Returns a normalized array with display name, coordinates (lat/lon), house number, road, city, state, postcode, and country.
  • Country code filtering — Limit search results to specific countries.
  • Language support — Set the preferred language for results.
  • Extensible provider system — Register your own address lookup providers via the address_lookup_for_acf/register_providers action.
  • REST API support — Field values are exposed in the REST API.
  • Photon provider — Use the Photon geocoding service as an alternative to Nominatim.

Usage

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Create or edit an ACF field group.
  3. Add a new field and select the Address field type.
  4. Optionally configure country code filtering and language.
  5. Use get_field() or the_field() in your templates — the value is returned as an associative array.

Template example

$address = get_field('my_address_field');

The returned array has the following structure:

[
    'display_name'  => 'Example Street 1, City, Country',
    'coordinates'   => ['lat' => '52.370216', 'lon' => '4.895168'],
    'house_number'  => '1',
    'street'        => 'Example Street',
    'city'          => 'City',
    'state'         => 'State',
    'postcode'      => '1234 AB',
    'country'       => 'Country',
]

Custom providers

You can register a custom address lookup provider by hooking into the jk_address_lookup_for_acf/register_providers action:

add_action('jk_address_lookup_for_acf/register_providers', function ($registry) {
    $registry->register(new MyCustomProvider());
});

Your provider must extend justinkruit\AddressLookupForAcf\Providers\AbstractProvider and implement the name(), label(), and search() methods.

Filters

  • jk_address_lookup_for_acf/nominatim_url — Override the Nominatim API base URL (e.g. to use a self-hosted instance).
  • jk_address_lookup_for_acf/nominatim_url_vars — Modify the query parameters sent to the Nominatim API.
  • jk_address_lookup_for_acf/photon_url — Override the Photon API base URL (e.g. to use a self-hosted instance).
  • jk_address_lookup_for_acf/photon_url_vars — Modify the query parameters sent to the Photon API.

Both filters also support ACF’s field-specific variations by type, name, and key.

External services

This plugin connects to third-party external services to perform address lookups. No data is sent automatically; requests are only made when an admin user actively searches for an address in the ACF field editor. The search query text is sent to the configured provider’s API.

Below is a list of each provider, what additional data is sent, how to override the API URL, and links to their terms and privacy policies.

Nominatim (OpenStreetMap)

Service: Nominatim by the OpenStreetMap Foundation: used for geocoding address searches.

Additional data sent: configured country code(s) and language preference (if set in the field settings).

Override URL: use the jk_address_lookup_for_acf/nominatim_url filter to point to a self-hosted instance.

Policies:

  • Nominatim Usage Policy
  • OpenStreetMap Foundation Terms of Use
  • OpenStreetMap Foundation Privacy Policy

Photon

Service: Photon by Komoot: used for geocoding address searches, powered by OpenStreetMap data.

Additional data sent: configured country code(s) and language preference (if set in the field settings).

Override URL: use the jk_address_lookup_for_acf/photon_url filter to point to a self-hosted instance.

Policies:

  • Photon Terms of Service
  • Komoot Privacy Policy

plugins.name: European VAT Compliance Assistant for WooCommerce
plugins.author: David Anderson / Team Updraft
plugins.short_description: Assists with EU/UK/Norway/Switzerland VAT compliance for WooCommerce, for the VAT regimes that began in 2015 and were extended in 2021), including the …
plugins.description:
The European/UK VAT (IVA) laws

Since January 1st 2015, all digital goods (including electronic, telecommunications, software, ebook and broadcast services), and from 1st July 2021 physical goods sold across EU and UK borders have been liable under law to variable VAT (a.k.a. IVA) charged in the country of purchase, at the VAT rate of that country (background information: https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2016-09/explanatory_notes_2015_en.pdf). This can apply even if the seller is not based in the EU or UK. It is accompanied by various auditing/recording requirements.

How this plugin can take away the pain

This WooCommerce plugin provides features to assist with EU, UK, Norwegian and Swiss VAT law compliance. Currently, those features include:

  • Identify your customers’ locations: this plugin will record evidence of your customer’s location, using their billing or shipping address, and their IP address (via a GeoIP lookup).

  • Evidence is recorded, ready for audit: full information that was used to calculate VAT and customer location is displayed in the WooCommerce order screen in the back-end.

  • Display prices including correct VAT from the first page: GeoIP information is also used to show the correct VAT from the first time a customer sees a product. A widget and shortcode are also provided allowing the customer to set their own country.

  • Currency conversions: Most users (if not everyone) will be required to report VAT information in a specific currency. This may be a different currency from their shop currency. This feature causes conversion rate information to be stored together with the order, at order time. Currently, you can choose from official rates from the European Central Bank (ECB), Danish and Czech National Banks, the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, and HM Customs & Revenue (UK). You can also over-ride the currency and rate-provider on a per-country basis.

  • Entering and maintaining each country’s VAT rates: this plugin assists with entering EU and/or UK VAT rates accurately by supplying a single button to press in your WooCommerce tax rates settings, to add or update rates for all countries (standard or reduced) with one click.

  • Reporting: Advanced reporting capabilities, allowing you to see all the information needed to make a OSS/MOSS/IOSS (one-stop shop) VAT report. The report is sortable and broken down by country, VAT rate, VAT type (traditional/variable) and order status, and can be exported as a CSV.

  • Forbid vatable sales if any goods have VAT chargeable – for shop owners for whom VAT compliance is too burdensome, this feature will allow you to forbid customers from configured VAT territories to check-out if they have selected any goods which are subject to VAT (whilst still allowing purchase of other goods, unlike the built-in WooCommerce feature which allows you to forbid check-out from some countries entirely).

  • Central control: brings all settings, reports and other information into a single centralised location, so that you don’t have to deal with items spread all over the WordPress dashboard.

  • Mixed shops: You can sell goods subject to your chosen territories’ VAT under the customer-place-of-supply regulations and any other physical goods which are subject to traditional base-country-based VAT regulations. The plugin supports this via allowing you to identify which tax classes in your WooCommerce configuration are used for customer-place-of-supply items. Products are allocated to the correct country according to which country VAT is payable to.

  • Distinguish VAT from other taxes: if you are in a jurisdiction where you have to apply other taxes also, then this plugin can correctly distinguish which taxes are payable to which jurisdictions.

  • Add line to invoices: If VAT was paid on the order, then an extra, configurable line can be added to the footer of the PDF invoice (when using the the free WooCommerce PDF invoices and packing slips plugin, or its premium counterpart).

  • Refund support: includes information on refunded VAT, on relevant orders.

  • Same prices: Not strictly a VAT compliance issue (different pricing per-country is not illegal), but this plugin adds an option to enable WooCommerce’s hidden support for adjusting pre-tax prices to enable the same post-tax (net) price to apply in all customer locations.

  • Brexit-ready: The plugin has been audited and appropriately adapted to be usable by both “EU 27” and UK (and other) countries after the expiry of the EU and UK’s transitional period (at the end of December 2020), including the ability to report taxes in multiple currencies using different exchange rate providers. Existing users should take the time to go through their existing settings to adapt to their new situation (e.g. remove tax table entries for countries that they are no longer required to remit taxes to; check that they are using the correct exchange rate provider and reporting currency for each tax region that they remit to).

  • WooCommerce high-performance order storage: This plugin is HPOS-compatible (see: https://woocommerce.com/document/high-performance-order-storage/)

  • WooCommerce block cart/checkout: This plugin is compatible with the WooCommerce block cart and checkout (see: https://woocommerce.com/checkout-blocks/), as well as the traditional shortcode cart/checkout.

A Premium version is on sale at this link, and currently has these additional features ready:

  • VAT-registered buyers can be exempted, and their numbers validated: a VAT number can be entered at the check-out, and it will be validated (via VIES, HMRC or VatSense). Qualifying customers can then be exempted from VAT on their purchase, and their information recorded. The customer’s VAT number will be appended to the billing address where shown (e.g. order summary email, PDF invoices). An extra, configurable line specific to this situation can be added to the footer of the PDF invoice (when using the the free WooCommerce PDF invoices and packing slips plugin).

  • Partial VAT exemption: make VAT-exemption upon supply of a valid VAT number to only apply to products in tax classes specified by the shop owner (rather than to all products)

  • Optionally allow B2B sales only – for shop owners who wish to only make sales that are VAT-exempt (i.e. B2B sales only), you can require that any EU and/or UK customers (optionally including or excluding those in your country) enter a valid VAT number at the check-out. (You can have different policies for different VAT regions).

  • Change taxation rules based upon year-to-date sales thresholds: for shop owners who can or must tax differently based upon their total sales in the year so far (e.g. EU shop owners who can take advantage of a €10,000 threshold for cross-border sales before which they can treat the place of supply as being their own, not the customer’s location), you can dynamically treat products as having a different taxation class until this threshold is met.

  • CSV download: A CSV containing comprehensive information on all orders with VAT data from your configured regions can be downloaded (including full compliance information). Manipulate in your spreadsheet program to make arbitrary calculations.

  • Non-contradictory evidences: require two non-contradictory evidences of location (if the customer address and GeoIP lookup contradict, then the customer will be asked to self-certify his location, by choosing between them).

  • Show multiple currencies for VAT taxes on PDF invoices produced by the free WooCommerce PDF invoices and packing slips plugin (and on credit notes produced by its Premium counterpart).

  • Support for the official WooCommerce subscriptions extension, and for Subscriptio (a RightPress/CodeCanyon alternative), and Subscriben.

  • Value-based exemption: An order can have VAT removed if the order value passes a configured value and is for a specified country. This features was developed to support the UK’s 2021 regulations for handling VAT differently on an order depending on whether or not the order passes a £135 threshold value, and then expanded to support multiple rules for different countries and amounts.

Read more about the Premium version of this plugin at this link.

It is believed (but not legally guaranteed), that armed with the above capabilities, a WooCommerce shop owner will be in a position to fulfil the requirements of EU or UK VAT laws: identifying the customer’s location and collecting multiple pieces of evidence, applying the correct VAT rate, validating VAT numbers for B2B transactions, and having the data needed to create returns. (If in the EU or UK, then you will also need to make sure that you are issuing your customers with VAT invoices containing the information required in your jurisdiction, via a suitable WooCommerce invoice plugin).

Footnotes and legalese

This plugin is supported on, and information in this document is for, WooCommerce 4.5 up to the latest release (i.e. current version; you can still download older versions supporting previous WooCommerce release series if you wish). It fetches data on current VAT rates from Amazon S3 (using SSL if possible); or, upon failure to connect to Amazon S3, from https://raw.githubusercontent.com. If your server’s firewall does not permit this, then it will use static data contained in the plugin.

Geographical IP lookups are performed via WooCommerce’s built-in geo-location features; or, alternatively, if you use CloudFlare, then you can activate the CloudFlare feature for sending geographical information. In some situations, these lookups may be performed via the public API at https://ipapi.co – if this is undesirable for you, then add define('WC_VAT_COMPLIANCE_DO_REMOTE_IP_LOOKUPS', false); to your wp-config.php file.

Please make sure that you review this plugin’s installation instructions and have not missed any important information there.

Please note that, just as with WordPress and its plugins generally (including WooCommerce), this plugin comes with no warranty of any kind and you deploy it entirely at your own risk. Furthermore, nothing in this plugin (including its documentation) constitutes legal or financial or any other kind of advice of any sort. In particular, you remain completely and solely liable for your own compliance with all taxation laws and regulations at all times, including research into what you must comply with. Installing any version of this plugin does not absolve you of any legal liabilities, or transfer any liabilities of any kind to us, and we provide no guarantee that use of this plugin will cover everything that your store needs to be able to do.

Whether you think the EU’s treaties with other jurisdictions will lead to success in enforcing the collection of taxes in other jurisdictions is a question for lawyers and potential tax-payers, not for software developers!

Many thanks to Diego Zanella, for various ideas we have swapped whilst working on these issues. Thanks to Dietrich Ayala and other authors, whose NuSOAP library is included under the LGPLv2 licence.

Other information

  • Some other WooCommerce plugins you may be interested in

  • This plugin is ready for translations (English, Dutch, Finnish, French and German are currently available), and we would welcome new translations (please post them in the support forum; the POT file is here, or you can contact us and ask for a web-based login for our translation website).
